config.title: Multiple State Variables

intro.title: Multiple State Variables
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Vue application that manages multiple independent pieces of reactive state. You will learn how to declare and use several separate ref() variables to track different data, like a user's name and age. The core concept is understanding how Vue's reactivity system can handle multiple state variables simultaneously within a single component. You will work with the ref() function from Vue's Composition API and bind these variables to different elements in the template. By the end, you'll have a functional app that updates and displays multiple data points independently.
intro.usecase: In real-world Vue applications, managing multiple state variables is essential for handling complex user interfaces. For example, in an e-commerce product page, you might need separate reactive variables for product details, user selections like size and color, quantity in cart, and inventory status—all updating independently as users interact. Dashboard interfaces commonly use multiple state variables to track different data sets, filter selections, and UI states like expanded panels or active tabs. This pattern allows developers to build responsive, modular components where each piece of state can be updated without affecting unrelated parts of the interface.

objectives: Initialize multiple reactive state variables in a Vue component
Apply separate computed properties derived from distinct state variables
Construct multiple event handlers that update different state variables
Bind multiple state variables to corresponding form inputs in the template
Manipulate independent state variables through separate user interactions
Render dynamic content based on the combined values of multiple state variables
Configure a component with multiple state variables that maintain independent reactivity

steps.title: Import Vue and ref from vue
steps.instruction: Import Vue and the ref function from the 'vue' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in Vue and ref from the vue module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing from a package
import { createApp, ref } from 'vue'
steps.seedCode: // Import Vue and ref from 'vue' here
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have the necessary imports to use Vue's reactivity system with ref.
successCriteria: Vue and ref are imported from the 'vue' package.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing both Vue and ref from the 'vue' package.
steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. You need to import Vue and ref from the 'vue' package to proceed.

steps.title: Create the Vue component structure
steps.instruction: Create a Vue component named MultipleStateExample with template and script sections. The component should return a basic template structure.
steps.hint: In Vue, a component typically has a template section for HTML markup and a script section for JavaScript logic.
steps.seedCode:
import { ref } from 'vue'

// Create your Vue component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A Vue component named MultipleStateExample is created with template and script sections.
successCriteria: The component is named MultipleStateExample and includes both template and setup sections.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your component has both template and setup sections.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've created a Vue component with the correct structure. Remember to include both template and script sections.

steps.title: Initialize the first state variable
steps.instruction: Inside your Vue component, declare a reactive state variable named 'count' using ref with an initial value of 0.
steps.hint: Use const count = ref(0) to create a reactive state variable that tracks a numeric count.
steps.analogousExample:
// Creating a reactive state variable
const score = ref(100)
steps.expectedOutcome: A reactive count variable is initialized with value 0, ready to be used in the component.
successCriteria: The component contains a count variable declared with ref(0).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using ref(0) to initialize the count variable.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try again. Remember to declare a variable named 'count' using ref with initial value 0.

steps.title: Initialize the second state variable
steps.instruction: Declare a second reactive state variable called 'name' using ref, initialized with an empty string. Place this declaration after your existing 'count' variable.
steps.hint: Use the same ref function you imported earlier. The syntax is: const name = ref('')
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: declaring a reactive variable
const message = ref('Hello')
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have two independent reactive state variables: count and name.
successCriteria: A 'name' variable is declared using ref with an empty string initial value
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're using ref() with an empty string as the initial value, and the variable should be named 'name'.
steps.feedbackWrong: declare a variable called 'name' using the ref function with an empty string initial value.

steps.title: Create handler to update count
steps.instruction: Create a function named increment that increases the count state variable by 1.
steps.hint: Define a function that accesses count.value and increments it by 1.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named increment that modifies the count state variable.
successCriteria: The increment function is defined and correctly increases count.value by 1.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a function, but make sure it correctly increments count.value by 1.
steps.feedbackWrong: The increment function is missing or doesn't modify count.value correctly.

steps.title: Create handler to update name
steps.instruction: Create a function named updateName that updates the name state variable to a new value. The function should accept a newName parameter and set name.value to that parameter.
steps.hint: Define a function that takes a parameter and assigns it to name.value. Remember that name will be a ref variable.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have an updateName function that can modify the name state variable when called.
successCriteria: The updateName function is defined, takes a newName parameter, and sets name.value to that parameter.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started creating the updateName function, but it needs to properly accept a parameter and update name.value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The updateName function isn't defined correctly. Make sure it accepts a newName parameter and sets name.value to that value.

steps.title: Add template structure with container
steps.instruction: Add a template section to your component with a div container element.
steps.hint: In Vue components, the template section defines the HTML structure. Add <template> with a <div> inside.
steps.analogousExample: // Adding a template section
steps.expectedOutcome: Your component will have a basic template structure with a container div ready for content.
successCriteria: The component has a template section containing a div element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added both the <template> tags and a <div> element inside them.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template structure isn't complete yet. Remember to add both the <template> tags and a <div> element inside.

steps.title: Display the count state
steps.instruction: Add a paragraph element inside the template's div that displays the current count value using interpolation.
steps.hint: Use double curly braces {{ }} to output the value of count in the template.
steps.analogousExample: // Displaying a reactive value in Vue template
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will show a paragraph with the current count value (initially 0).
successCriteria: A paragraph element exists inside the div and displays the count value using interpolation.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you added a paragraph element and used interpolation to show the count value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The paragraph element with the count value is missing or incorrect. Check the template structure and interpolation syntax.

steps.title: Add button to increment count and wire click handler
steps.instruction: Add a button element inside the template that calls the increment function when clicked.
steps.hint: Use the @click directive to attach the increment function to the button's click event.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a button with click handler
<button @click="increment">Increment</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will contain a button that, when clicked, triggers the increment function to update the count state.
successCriteria: A button element with @click="increment" is added to the template.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a button, but it's not wired to the increment function yet. Make sure to use @click="increment".
steps.feedbackWrong: The button is missing or not properly connected to the increment function. Add a button with @click="increment".

steps.instruction: Add a paragraph to display the name state value and an input field bound to the name state using v-model.

Use

steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will display the current name value and provide an input field that updates the name state when typed into.
successCriteria: A paragraph displays the name state value and an input field with v-model="name" is added to the template.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have both the paragraph showing the name value and the input field with v-model.
